common_mixture_extension.hypothesis: One common positive-order minimum-mixture with generating function F(s)=sum_(m>=1) a_m s^m, a_m>=0, sum a_m=1. Coefficients may depend on t and on the entire input family, but not on output index or coordinate.

common_mixture_extension.case_one: If H(M)<=1/2, concavity gives every secant slope on[0,M] at least(1-H(M))/(1-M)>=1/2. With every-edge l1 separation>=1/3, variation forces C^2>=t/144.
common_mixture_extension.case_two: If H(M)>1/2, concavity gives sum_k H(G_ik)>=H(M)/M>1/(2M). Exact input-output distance is [sumH+1-2H(G_ii)]/(n-1)>=[sumH-1]/(n-1). For M<=1/4 this forces C^2>=1/(64 M^2).
common_mixture_extension.conclusion: No such common minimum-mixture gives a uniform cotype estimate, even with adaptive common coefficients. This is a failure of these prescribed operators, not a lower bound on optimal feasible witnesses, universal coupling, or the full extension theorem.
